summary: Independent, owner-operated outpatient physical therapy clinic in Old Bridge, NJ, serving the community since 1996 with orthopedic, geriatric, vestibular/balance, sports rehab, manual, shockwave and ultrasound therapy at a single Woodward Drive location. The clinic runs on a WordPress/Divi site with GoHighLevel-based chat and embedded third-party intake forms, but no visible online scheduling or patient portal, and its own careers page shows it is actively hiring a full-time physical therapist. All review evidence available is first-party (the site's claim of 85+ five-star ratings and curated testimonials); third-party review and job-board pages were blocked during research.

facts.fact: Single location at 14 Woodward Drive, Suite B, Old Bridge, NJ 08857, with phone (732) 360-1100, fax (732) 360-1170 and email info@cjpta.com.
Clinic hours are Mon/Wed/Fri 7:00 AM-5:00 PM, Tue/Thu 8:00 AM-6:00 PM, Sat 7:30 AM-12:00 PM.
The practice states it has served Old Bridge and surrounding towns since 1996 (elsewhere described as over 25 years).
Service lines listed include geriatric PT, orthopedic therapy, general physical therapy, sports rehab, vestibular therapy, manual therapy, shockwave therapy and ultrasound.
Stated in-network with Medicare, Horizon Blue Cross Blue Shield, United Health, Cigna, Oxford, and motor vehicle/workers comp plans.
Team page lists four physical therapists (Ajay Kalola, Minal Kalola, Hardikkumar Unjia, Danielle Luksa), two PTAs (David Dezenzo, Joseph Maag) and one admin staff member (Connor Harkins).
Ajay Kalola graduated from SUNY Health Science Center at Brooklyn in 1996, is specialty-trained in vestibular PT and is a certified clinical instructor for DPT students.
Careers page advertises a full-time licensed physical therapist for the Old Bridge location with medical/dental/vision, 401k, PTO, CEU reimbursement, flexible scheduling and a mentorship program.
Homepage claims a 5-star Google rating, a 5-star Yelp rating and more than 85 five-star reviews.
Appointment requests are collected through an embedded third-party form widget (link.rehabceos.com), not a scheduling calendar.
Staff verify insurance benefits by calling the patient's plan before the first appointment so exact benefits can be quoted.
Site is built on WordPress with the Divi theme and Yoast SEO, and loads a LeadConnector (GoHighLevel) chat/SMS widget plus Google Analytics via Site Kit.

operations_signals: No self-service online booking: prospective patients either call or submit an embedded web form and wait for staff follow-up (https://cjpta.com/request-an-appointment/).
Insurance verification is a manual, staff-run step: the office takes plan details by phone, calls the insurer, then quotes benefits before the first visit (https://cjpta.com/insurance/).
Website chat widget is configured for email/SMS chat with copy promising 'a care coordinator will get right back to you', including consent language for SMS/email replies (https://cjpta.com/).
New-patient paperwork is collected through a second embedded third-party form rather than a patient portal (https://cjpta.com/paperwork/).
Bill payment is split across an online card payment link, mailed statements, and phone payments during business hours only (https://cjpta.com/pay-my-bill/).
Hours stop at 5-6 PM on weekdays and 12 PM Saturday, with Sunday closed and no published after-hours or emergency line (https://cjpta.com/request-an-appointment/).
FAQ notes New Jersey direct access, so patients can self-refer without a physician prescription, which widens the front-door intake funnel (https://cjpta.com/).
Single clinic location serving Old Bridge and surrounding towns; no satellite offices appear anywhere in the site's sitemap (https://cjpta.com/sitemap.xml).
hiring_signals: Open full-time licensed physical therapist role posted on the clinic's own careers page for the Old Bridge location (https://cjpta.com/hiring-pt/).
Posting emphasizes 'growth-minded', 'growing team' and a long-term hire, plus benefits and a structured mentorship program with unlimited CEUs (https://cjpta.com/hiring-pt/).
No administrative, front-desk, billing or scheduling postings were found; the staff page shows a single admin role covering the clinic (https://cjpta.com/staff/).

Job duties described are clinical (evaluations, patient engagement, collaboration) rather than operational, so hiring does not appear aimed at relieving front-office load (https://cjpta.com/hiring-pt/).
review_themes: Practice advertises 85+ five-star reviews and 5-star Google and Yelp ratings, but the underlying review pages could not be opened for verification (https://cjpta.com/).
Curated testimonials repeatedly praise being greeted by name and treated 'like family' rather than as a case number (https://cjpta.com/testimonial/).
Reviewers highlight owners being hands-on on the floor and monitoring all patients at once (https://cjpta.com/testimonial/).
One reviewer notes 'no wait between exercises' and a wide variety of equipment, implying session flow and equipment capacity matter to patients (https://cjpta.com/testimonial/).
Testimonials stress listening and communication from the moment a patient walks in, suggesting responsiveness is a competitive strength (https://cjpta.com/testimonial/).
No critical or mixed reviews appear on the clinic's own testimonial page; all displayed quotes are five-star, so complaint themes could not be assessed (https://cjpta.com/testimonial/).
tech_footprint: WordPress CMS with Divi theme (v4.27.9) and Yoast SEO (v28.7); pages last modified 2026 in the markup (https://cjpta.com/).
LeadConnector / GoHighLevel chat and SMS widget installed, carrying agency branding for 'PT Marketing Secrets' with text-widget location ID configured (https://cjpta.com/).
Google Analytics 4 via Site Kit (tag GT-5D96W2CX) on all pages (https://cjpta.com/).
Appointment and patient-form embeds hosted at link.rehabceos.com, a third-party therapy-marketing form platform (https://cjpta.com/request-an-appointment/).
No online scheduling calendar, patient portal, or insurance/benefits self-check tool observed anywhere on the site (https://cjpta.com/insurance/).
No blog or resource library: the sitemap contains only service, condition, staff, testimonial and utility pages, so published content is thin (https://cjpta.com/sitemap.xml).
Sitemap and page timestamps show active SEO maintenance, with pages re-touched in late 2026 (https://cjpta.com/sitemap.xml).
growth_signals: Actively recruiting a full-time PT while describing itself as a 'growing team', indicating capacity expansion rather than contraction (https://cjpta.com/hiring-pt/).
Service mix has expanded beyond core orthopedics into shockwave therapy, vestibular/balance, fall prevention and pre/post-natal PT (https://cjpta.com/services/).
Positioning targets Medicare and post-joint-replacement patients, a growing demographic in the Old Bridge area (https://cjpta.com/).

No additional locations, acquisitions, awards or press coverage could be verified; the site references being 'provider of choice for the local medical community' without naming referral sources (https://cjpta.com/).
decision_maker: Ajay Kalola, LPT / physical therapist and co-owner (site staff page lists him as Physical Therapist; a patient testimonial on the clinic's site refers to 'the owner physical therapists, Ajay and Minal') — https://cjpta.com/staff/ajay-kalola/ and https://cjpta.com/testimonial/

inferences.inference: Front-office work is concentrated in very few hands, likely one admin plus the owners.
inferences.reasoning: The staff page lists seven clinical staff and one admin (Connor Harkins), while intake, insurance verification, scheduling and billing are all described as staff-handled phone/web-form processes.

inferences.inference: Insurance benefit checks are a high-volume, repetitive manual task and a likely automation target.
inferences.reasoning: The clinic states it calls each patient's insurer before the first appointment 'without any exception' to confirm in-network status and quote exact benefits.

inferences.inference: Intake data is probably re-keyed by hand into a practice-management system.
inferences.reasoning: Appointment requests and patient forms are collected in embedded third-party form widgets with no visible EMR/portal integration or scheduling calendar.

inferences.inference: Leads are likely lost outside business hours and on weekends.
inferences.reasoning: There is no online scheduling, hours end at 5-6 PM weekdays and noon Saturday, and the only after-hours channel is a chat widget routed to staff.

inferences.inference: Review generation is probably ad hoc rather than automated.
inferences.reasoning: The site advertises 85+ five-star reviews accumulated over roughly 29 years, and no review-request or reputation tooling was visible in the page source.

inferences.inference: Growth depends on physician referral relationships rather than inbound marketing.
inferences.reasoning: The site claims to be the 'provider of choice for the local medical community', publishes no blog content, and lists no paid-ad or lead-nurture tooling beyond the chat widget and analytics.

inferences.inference: The clinic's marketing is outsourced to a therapy-specific agency, which may limit in-house control of follow-up workflows.
inferences.reasoning: The chat widget embeds agency branding for 'PT Marketing Secrets' and intake forms are hosted on link.rehabceos.com.

data_gaps: Google Business Profile and Yelp review pages were unreachable (JavaScript-rendered or HTTP 403), so review count, rating, recency and complaint themes are unverified beyond the clinic's own claims.
Indeed, ZipRecruiter and LinkedIn job/company pages returned HTTP 403, so current and historical postings beyond the clinic's own careers page could not be checked.
BBB and Healthgrades did not surface a profile for this practice, so accreditation, complaint history and provider-level ratings are unknown.
The practice-management/EMR and billing software in use was not identifiable from public pages.
Employee headcount, revenue, patient volume and payer mix are not publicly disclosed.
No local news, press coverage, awards or expansion announcements could be located; web search providers were rate-limited or blocked during this research.
